view.headline: The week was a hardware-versus-software split, not a broad-tape move and not a risk-off week

sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
## The week was a hardware-versus-software split, not a broad-tape move and not a risk-off week

For the week ended 2026-09-04, SPY returned +0.1% (rotation, benchmarkReturns w1) — essentially flat. That flatness is the story's disguise: beneath it, silicon-and-metal leadership diverged sharply from software, so this was not a broad rally (the index barely moved), not a risk-off week (VIXCLS eased to 14.32 from a prior 15.20, a -0.88-pt move as of 2026-09-03; high-yield spread BAMLH0A0HYM2 tightened to 2.65 from 2.66), and not a rate-driven repricing (DGS10 slipped only -2 bp to 4.77 as of 2026-09-03). What moved was sector dispersion.

## Memory and hardware led; enterprise software and security lagged, on the same flat tape

The widest sector spreads sat at opposite poles. Memory/Storage gained +7.5% vs SPY (all 4 of 4 members, as of 2026-09-04), the frame's largest positive sector excess, with SNDK the single strongest name at +17.06% excess vs SPY over the 2026-08-31–2026-09-04 window (coverageCandidates, rank 1). Computer/GPU added +5.7% vs SPY (6 of 6) and Foundry +5.3% (4 of 4), DELL contributing +14.77% excess vs SPY (rank 3). Against that, Cybersecurity fell -7.0% vs SPY (4 of 4), the frame's largest negative sector excess, and Software/SaaS -4.8% (6 of 6); PANW printed -10.42% and FIG -16.42% excess vs SPY (ranks 6 and 2). The plausible mechanism is an AI-buildout tilt — capacity and components bid, application-layer names sold — but relative outperformance alone does not identify the cause, and I flag this as judgement: the flat index and unchanged rates are consistent with a rotation inside tech rather than a macro driver. Confirming: Memory/Storage holds a positive weekly excess in the next rotation read dated after 2026-09-04. Refuting: Cybersecurity's -7.0% excess reverses to positive next week, which would mark this as a one-week unwind, not a trend.

## Energy and ag inputs outran the tape across every horizon

The el-nino-ag basket (DBA, MOS, NTR, DE equal-weight) returned +6.6% for the week, +6.5% excess over SPY (theme row, week.excessPct 6.5167, as of 2026-09-04), and carried it across windows: excess4w +13.3, excess12w +11.6 (rotation). XLE confirmed the commodity lean with +2.1% excess1w, +11.8% excess4w and +8.0% excess12w. WTI crude rose to 94.09 (+2.85%) while gold eased to 4400.645 (-0.66%) as of 2026-09-08 — note that commodity level is a post-window snapshot, not a weekly change. Within the basket, DE (+9.92%) and MOS (+9.42% excess vs SPY, ranks 7 and 8) carried the ag inputs. The theme's declared trigger is NOAA ONI ≥ +0.5 for three consecutive months and CBOT corn/wheat vs 20-day; both are operator-checked and I have no dated reading for either input this week, so I cannot state the trigger is met — the price move is real, the fundamental confirmation is unverified here. Confirming: the basket holds positive weekly excess in the rotation read dated after 2026-09-04. Refuting: the basket's excess turns negative, or a dated ONI print lands below +0.5.

Limitation: the dated close-report archive and the headline feed both returned empty for this run (ow_reports, ow_uw_headlines as-of 2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z), so this week carries no narrative citations beyond the priced frame and rotation tables; equity internals and commodities levels are post-window snapshots dated 2026-09-08 and are not weekly changes.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
The clearest question into next week is whether the hardware-over-software split is a durable AI-capacity rotation or a one-week dispersion that mean-reverts. The bull case rests on breadth: Memory/Storage (+7.5% vs SPY), Computer/GPU (+5.7%) and Foundry (+5.3%) all moved with every member participating (4/4, 6/6, 4/4), which is harder to dismiss as single-name noise than a narrow move would be. It persists if those excesses stay positive in the next rotation read; it invalidates if Cybersecurity's -7.0% and Software/SaaS's -4.8% excesses snap back, which would recast this week as an unwind. Reverse risk: a sharp software recovery would pull the flat index the other way with the same tape.

The macro backdrop is quiet and gives the rotation room. DGS10 at 4.77 (-2 bp), high-yield at 2.65 (-1 bp) and VIXCLS at 14.32 (-0.88 pts) are all calm as of 2026-09-03 — but I read these as observations, not evidence of complacency or of what is priced. The one live policy datum is the 9/16 hike probability at 55.7 (as of 2026-09-04); the frame excludes it from ranking for lack of a prior, so I can quote the level but not a direction of travel. That FOMC decision is 2026-09-16 — later context, beyond the coming seven days, not a next-week pivot.

The energy and ag-input leadership is the most persistent feature: el-nino-ag +6.5% excess this week stacks on +13.3% (4w) and +11.6% (12w), and XLE echoes it across all three windows. Multi-horizon consistency argues for continuation over a one-week spike. It persists if crude holds its bid and the basket keeps positive weekly excess; it fades if a dated ONI reading comes in below +0.5 or the basket underperforms SPY, which is the theme's own armed kill condition. Reverse risk: a crude reversal would hit XLE and the ag complex together.

Into the ADBE print on 2026-09-10, the software-lagging tape is the frame for a name whose sector fell -4.8% vs SPY this week; the read-through to the wider Software/SaaS group matters more than the single reaction. Watch whether one soft print deepens the group's relative weakness or whether the sector was already discounting it.
